messages:
morgan: heads up — ran the nightly onboarding eval for petrel-v1 (fp16 vs int4) on staging and we have a nasty regression on a few locale slices, esp CJK context boundaries and RTL Arabic->en translation. sample summary below.

anika: ugh. numbers? config?

morgan: quick paste:
```
model: petrel-v1
precision: int4 (dynamic range)
datasets: multilingual-simbench-v2 (zh->en, ja->en, ar->en, he->en)
batch: 8
seed: 42
kernel: autotuned-qk-v2
metrics: BLEU, chrF, hallucination_rate (n-gram overlap w/refs), exact_token_mismatch_count
```
overall: zh->en BLEU -6.3 (fp16 28.1 -> int4 21.8), ja->en BLEU -4.1, ar->en BLEU -9.8. hallucination_rate ar->en +12.4% (relative).

lee: can you paste one small repro where tokenization/context looks off?

morgan: yes — isolated minimal example from the eval batch. note: this is not just fluency; model invents a location when asked about a follow-up question after a CJK linebreak.

INPUT (zh->en): 今天天气很好。
明天会下雨吗？
REF: Will it rain tomorrow?
FP16_OUT: It looks like rain is possible tomorrow.
INT4_OUT: The forecast says heavy rain in Shenzhen tomorrow — bring an umbrella.

tokenization (int4 run): ["今", "天天", "气", "很好", "。", "明天", "会", "下雨", "吗", "？"]
expected tokens: segmentation should not join day tokens across sentence boundary; seems we get an extra merge at the newline.

anika: that looks like a k-v cache / prefix handling issue — if tokens are merged incorrectly you can bleed context into the next segment and the model hallucinates specifics. did the kernel switch recently?

morgan: we flipped to autotuned-qk-v2 on 2026-02-18 in staging to get perf. logs show quantizer map changed for CJK unicode ranges. commit g4c2f9a toggles naive-byte-split fallback -> packed-unicode.

sanjay: pinging @lee — can you run a bisect between g4c2f9a and the previous autotune tag? also please check tokenizer table used during int4 export (we sometimes write a trimmed vocab for speed).

lee: running quick smoke now. also saw similar RTL symptom: short ar->en replies where punctuation normalization flips bracket orientation, then model appends a phrase unrelated to input when asked a follow-up question. sharing small ar example: 

INPUT (ar->en): هل يوجد مطار قريب؟
REF: Is there an airport nearby?
FP16_OUT: Yes, there is a small regional airport about 10 km away.
INT4_OUT: Yes, there is a small regional airport near Alexandria. You should check the local schedule.

anika: Alexandria is a hallucination for that prompt set — we don't have location data. seems like locale-specific priors are leaking when quantized.

eval-bot: automated-run: run_id=2026-03-19-3155, diffs: {zh_en: -6.3_BLEU, ja_en: -4.1_BLEU, ar_en: -9.8_BLEU, hallucination_rate_ar: +12.4%}. top-failing-examples attached to run artifact  s3://redwood-eval/petrel-v1/3155/failures.tar.gz

morgan: proposed short-term mitigation: 1) disable packed-unicode during quant export and re-run int4 export 2) enable stricter tokenization check in the export pipeline (reject exports where tokenization of dataset differs >0.5% from fp16 baseline) 3) rollback kernel on staging to autotuned-qk-v1 for canary.

sanjay: agree. also add a quick eval that masks out trailing named-entity spans to confirm it's entity leakage vs general fluency.

lee: smoke results: bisect points to g4c2f9a and the tokenizer trim step at export-time. when I force full vocab (no trimming) int4 reproduces much less.

anika: nice find. can we reproduce with a tiny script so infra can run nightly? if it's just vocab trimming, that's an easy patch for the release checklist.

morgan: I'll open a short PR to disable packed-unicode in the quant path and add the export-time tokenization parity check. will also attach the failing examples and the minimal repro script.

lee: created repro gist and queued a canary job on dedicated-staging. gist: https://gist.github.com/lee/petrel-int4-token-repro

eval-bot: canary queued: canary_id=canary-3155-tokenparity-01, expected runtime ~45m.

anika: thanks — if the canary passes we should include the tokenization parity check in the pre-release gate for petrel-v1. also add an eval slice for RTL punctuation orientation and short-context hallucination.

morgan: noted. will follow up with PR link and results once canary completes. :thumbsup:

sanjay: thanks team — triage looks actionable. keep notes in the petrel onboarding doc and link the run artifacts.

morgan: adding doc links in the PR. last: anyone want to add extra failing examples (small) to make the regression test more robust?

lee: dropping 6 more CJK and 4 AR examples into the artifact now.

anika: great. cc @eng-platform for canary scheduling if it needs extra GPU time.

morgan: end.
